Mr. Dushyant Mainali, learned counsel for 
petitioner.
2. Mr. Ashish Joshi, learned counsel for 
respondent Nos.1 and 2/PNB.
3. Mr. P.S. Bisht, learned Brief Holder for 
the State of Uttarakhand/respondent No.3.
4. This writ petition has been filed by 
petitioner-Society seeking a direction to 
respondent-Bank to forthwith defreeze bank 
account No.9964999199923668 of petitioner￾Society maintained with Punjab National 
Bank, Bhowali Branch, District Nainital.
5. It is contended by learned counsel for 
petitioner that the account of petitioner￾Society was freezed for want of renewal 
certificate which has now been submitted by 
petitioner-Society to the Branch on 
18.02.2026.
6. It is further contended by him that still 
the account has not been defreezed.
7. Learned counsel for respondent Nos.1 & 
2-PNB prays for and is granted 48 hrs. time to 
seek instruction in the matter.
8. Put up as fresh on 09.04.2026.
 (Pankaj Purohit, J.)

Hon’ble Pankaj Purohit, J.
Mr. Dushyant Mainali, learned counsel for the 
petitioner.
2. Mr. Ashish Joshi, learned counsel for respondent 
nos.1 & 2-PNB Bank.
3. Mr. Suyash Pant, learned Standing Counsel for the 
State/respondent no.3.
4. This writ petition was filed by the petitioner for a 
direction to the respondent-Bank to defreeze the Account 
No.9964999199923668 maintained in the PNB Bhowali
Branch, District Nainital.
5. This Court vide order dated 07.04.2026 asked 
learned counsel appearing for respondent nos.1 & 2-PNB 
as to why despite renewal certificate having been 
submitted by the petitioner, account has not been 
defreezed.
6. Today, though instructions have been received, but 
the instructions are incomprehensible and they are 
required to be clarified by the respondent-PNB.
7. Put up on 13.04.2026 as fresh enabling learned 
counsel for the respondent nos.1 & 2-PNB to explain the
instructions. 
(Pankaj Purohit, J.)
09.04.2026 AK 2

Mr. Dushyant Mainali, learned counsel for the petitioner.
2. Mr. Shobhit Joshi, learned counsel holding brief of Mr. 
Ashish Joshi, learned counsel for the respondent nos.1 & 2-
Bank.
3. Mr. Suyash Pant, learned Standing Counsel for the 
State/respondent no.3.
4. The amount of petitioner-Society was freezed on a 
complaint made by one Ms. Premila Saxena
5. The instructions were called from the respondent-Bank 
which has not satisfactory, therefore, again vide order dated 
09.04.2026, learned counsel for the respondent-Bank was 
directed to bring on record the clear instructions in the matter.
6. Today, instructions dated 10.04.2026 produced before this 
Court, which are taken on record. On the strength of 
instructions, it is submitted that the petitioner-Society is 
required to give the documents as enumerated in last para of the 
aforesaid instructions.
7. To this, learned counsel for the petitioner prays for and is 
granted a week’s time to provide the documents to the bank as 
enumerated in last para of the aforesaid instructions.
8. List on 24.04.2026 immediately after fresh cases. 
(Pankaj Purohit, J.)
